source:
🏉 Rugby Champions

Step onto the field and become a rugby legend! Pass, tackle, kick, score tries, and work with your teammates to win exciting matches.

Features

🏃 Sprint and dodge defenders. 

🤝 Pass the ball to teammates. 

💥 Tackle opponents to stop attacks. 

🥅 Kick conversions and penalty goals. 

🏆 Play 7v7 or 15v15 matches. 

💰 Earn coins after every match. 

🎽 Unlock new jerseys, boots, celebrations, and rugby balls. 

📈 Level up and improve your skills. 

Can you lead your team to victory and become the greatest rugby player?

Tutorial

When a player joins for the first time:

Welcome

Welcome to Rugby Champions! Your goal is to score more points than the other team.

Step 1 - Move

Use WASD to move. Hold Shift to sprint.

Player must walk to the highlighted marker.

Reward:

+50 Coins

Step 2 - Pick Up Ball

Walk over the rugby ball to pick it up.

Player touches the ball.

Step 3 - Pass

Press Q to pass to your teammate.

Player passes successfully.

Step 4 - Tackle

Press E near an opponent to tackle.

A practice dummy runs toward the player.

Step 5 - Score a Try

Run into the in-goal area while holding the ball.

Animation plays.

TRY! +5 Points

Step 6 - Conversion Kick

Aim using your mouse. Hold Left Click to build power. Release to kick.

Tutorial Complete

Congratulations! You are ready for online matches. Good luck!

Reward:

500 Coins 

Rookie Jersey 

Beginner Title 

Game Modes

Quick Match

Join instantly 

7v7 

Ranked

Competitive games 

Earn rank points 

Practice

AI opponents 

Learn controls 

Tournament

Large knockout competitions 

Controls

KeyActionWASDMoveShiftSprintQPassETackleSpaceJumpLeft ClickKickRDiveFCelebrate

Progression

Players earn:

Coins 

XP 

Jerseys 

Boots 

Ball skins 

Celebrations 

Titles 

Match Rules

Try = 5 points 

Conversion = 2 points 

Penalty Goal = 3 points 

Drop Goal = 3 points 

Match length: 10 minutes 

Team with the most points wins. 

Roblox Studio Structure

Workspace ├── RugbyField ├── Goals ├── Ball ├── SpawnLocations StarterPlayer ├── StarterCharacterScripts │ ├── Sprint │ ├── Tackle │ ├── BallPickup ReplicatedStorage ├── Remotes │ ├── PassBall │ ├── TacklePlayer │ ├── KickBall ServerScriptService ├── MatchManager ├── ScoreManager ├── TutorialManager ├── CoinRewards StarterGui ├── MainMenu ├── TutorialUI ├── Scoreboard ├── Shop ├── Settings

This design gives you a solid foundation for a polished Roblox rugby game with clear gameplay, a guided tutorial for new players, multiple game modes, progression, and a description suitable for the Roblox experience page. If you want to build it in Roblox Studio, I can also generate the Lua scripts for systems like ball handling, passing, tackling, scoring, matchmaking, and the tutorial.

answers.ask: Should this be a bare training pitch, a school ground, or a full floodlit professional stadium?
answers.answer: Use a full floodlit professional stadium to match the polished Rugby Champions experience.

answers.ask: Should the pitch be sized for 15v15, or tightened for 7v7?
answers.answer: Tighten the pitch for 7v7 as the primary quick-match format; 15v15 can remain a selectable mode without requiring a larger initial map.

scene_prompt: Create a 3D rugby match map set in a full floodlit professional stadium. Center the layout on a tightened rugby pitch sized for 7v7, with marked sidelines, halfway line, try lines, in-goal areas, and H-shaped goalposts at both ends. Place team spawn locations along opposite sides of the field, with the rugby ball at the center for play; stadium seating and bright floodlights frame the pitch.
blob:
### 1. Genre
The dominant genre is Sports: teams compete on a regulated rugby field to score tries and kicks. There is no secondary genre.

### 2. Shape and preset
Use `space-bounded`, the Sports Bounded Field or Court shape. It is a single, rigidly marked rugby pitch enclosed by a professional stadium. Match the Field Sport preset, with the prompt’s full floodlit stadium dressing added.

### 3. Config requirements
Use `trigger-bounds` for the marked touchlines, dead-ball limits, try lines, and in-goal boundaries defining active play. Use `startpoint-play` for the central restart position and the visible team starting sides. Use `trigger-scoring` for two in-goal scoring areas and the goalpost conversion targets. Use `marker-distance` for the halfway line and clear rugby field markings. Use `barrier-perimeter` as the stadium enclosure that contains play. Use `spectator-bleachers` as large tiered seating framing the pitch. The bright floodlight banks are part of the professional stadium dressing.

### 4. Layout requirements
Place `trigger-bounds` as continuous detection perimeters along both sidelines, both dead-ball lines, and the try-line/in-goal boundaries. Place `startpoint-play` once at midfield for the ball and as two opposing team start formations on either side of the halfway line. Place `trigger-scoring` in both in-goal areas, spanning the legal try-scoring ground and aligned to each H-shaped goalpost.

### 5. Layout components
The central zone is one tightened, rectangular 7v7 rugby pitch, with green turf, sidelines, halfway line, try lines, and two in-goal areas. H-shaped goalposts stand centered on the dead-ball line at each end. Opposing team spawn zones sit along opposite field sides, outside immediate contact space; the rugby ball begins precisely at pitch center. Tiered stadium seating wraps the long sides and ends beyond the boundary, with four bright floodlight arrays aimed inward. A continuous stadium wall and seating bowl enclose the map. Compose the pitch symmetrically in frame, with the halfway line as the central axis and both goals fully readable.

### 6. Render order
Use `topdown`: the marked field geometry, opposing spawn symmetry, and scoring boundaries must be spatially valid before the stadium is dressed isometrically.

### 7. Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is large, driven by a full professional stadium around a compact 7v7 pitch. Theme: polished floodlit rugby venue, vivid green turf, crisp white markings, and modern grandstands. Use `tiered` for stepped bleachers; otherwise use `P0`, since the stadium remains one connected surface and the seating does not overhang the pitch.
